slides.heading: Number Of Binary Tree Topologies
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Very Hard · Recursion
slides.narration: Let's solve Number Of Binary Tree Topologies, a very hard recursion problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Number of structurally distinct binary trees with n nodes (Catalan).
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Number of structurally distinct binary trees with n nodes (Catalan).

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Pick how many nodes go left; the counts multiply, giving the Catalan numbers.
slides.narration: Pick how many nodes go left; the counts multiply, giving the Catalan numbers.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
slides.narration: Plain recursion recomputes sizes. A DP over sizes is quadratic, and the answer is the Catalan number.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. For each n, sum left times right counts
slides.narration: Step by step. First, ways of zero is one. Second, for each n, sum left times right counts. Third, return ways of n.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 1 nodes → 1
slides.narration: With 1 nodes, choose how many go left; multiply the left and right counts and sum: 1.

slides.narration: With 2 nodes, choose how many go left; multiply the left and right counts and sum: 2.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: C of zero is one. For each m, sum c of left times c of m minus one minus left over all left sizes.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n squared. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: The empty tree counts as one topology.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Mention the closed form, two n choose n over n plus one.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Pick how many nodes go left; the counts multiply, giving the Catalan numbers.
slides.narration: To recap Number Of Binary Tree Topologies: Pick how many nodes go left; the counts multiply, giving the Catalan numbers. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
